findings.title: 28 classes of explorer.module.css belong to the former library page and no component uses them
findings.evidence: A CSS module class is only reachable as explorer / shared.<name> or explorer / shared["<name>"] in a file that imports explorer.module.css; a script listed every class of explorer.module.css, every importer and its alias, and every dynamic explorer / shared[...] index. Importers: entry.tsx, new-view.tsx, organisation.tsx and page.tsx (alias explorer), facet-page.tsx (alias shared); no dynamic index. Used classes: lead, primaryAction, count, empty, crumbs, eyebrow, facetStrip, facetChip, panel, reference. Unused classes with the line of their first rule: page (1), libraryHeader (6), toolbar (25), tabs (33, 39, 42-57), tabsAction (61), filters (75, 81), search (82, 90), group (97), groupTitle (102, 112), threadList (115), threadRow (124-135), threadLink (138, 149), threadHead (152), threadTitle (157), threadSummary (161), threadMeta (169), metaStrong (176), framework (180), pill (187), active (198), frozen (202), completed (206), cardGrid (210), card (215-237), cardTitle (241), activeThread (244), header (265), timeline (311-330), and the whole @media (max-width: 760px) block at lines 334-353, which only styles unused classes. Searched with rg over trust-extension/, apps/trust-web/acceptance/ and packages/: no file reaches these classes through explorer.module.css. Acceptance tests select by [class*='stepName'], [class*='icon'], [class*='tipDate'] and [class*='tipReason'] only, none of which matches these names. The thread list of the entry page is now rendered by thread-rows.tsx with entry.module.css.
findings.action: Delete the rules of the 28 unused classes and the @media (max-width: 760px) block from explorer.module.css; keep lead, primaryAction, count, empty, crumbs, eyebrow, facetStrip, facetChip, panel and reference.
findings.riskReason: CSS module class names are hashed, so no element can carry these classes unless a component names them, and none does; the remaining rules are untouched.
findings.stateReason: Deleted the rules of the 28 unused classes (page, libraryHeader, toolbar, tabs, tabsAction, filters, search, group, groupTitle, threadList, threadRow, threadLink, threadHead, threadTitle, threadSummary, threadMeta, metaStrong, framework, pill, active, frozen, completed, cardGrid, card, cardTitle, activeThread, header, timeline) and the @media (max-width: 760px) block from explorer.module.css; lead, primaryAction, count, empty, crumbs, eyebrow, facetStrip, facetChip, panel and reference are kept.

findings.title: thread-status.ts repeats the thread state labels that threadState in visual-language.tsx already defines

also.text: import type { Thread } from "./types";

? t(threadStatus({ state: key as ThreadState }))

import { threadStatus } from "./thread-status";
[t("State"), filters.states.map((state) => t(threadStatus({ state }))).join(", ") || all],

findings.evidence: Both switch over the thread state and return the same English labels: In progress, Open, Paused and Completed, with the same error for an unknown state. threadStatus feeds the state filter of entry.tsx and the summary of new-view.tsx; threadState feeds the state pills (ThreadStatePill). Searched with rg over trust-extension/, apps/trust-web/acceptance/ and packages/: no other definition of these labels in ui/.
findings.action: Make entry.tsx and new-view.tsx use threadState(thread, state === "IN_PROGRESS").label from visual-language.tsx (or a small wrapper exported from it) and delete thread-status.ts.
findings.riskReason: threadState takes the ACTIVE state plus an atWork flag while threadStatus takes the synthetic IN_PROGRESS state; the mapping must keep the filter labels identical, and the filter of entry.tsx is covered by browser tests only.
findings.stateReason: Fixed by the coordinator's arbitration. Deleted thread-status.ts and its duplicated switch (the cited lines) with its import of Thread (also entry). entry.tsx (state filter options and state group titles) and new-view.tsx (state summary) now call listStateLabel, exported from visual-language.tsx next to threadState: IN_PROGRESS is threadState({ state: ACTIVE }, true).label, the other states threadState({ state }).label, so the labels stay In progress, Open, Paused and Completed, in the order of STATES. The also entries are the 2 removed imports of thread-status and the 3 replaced threadStatus calls.
